root_cause.text: During filesystem shutdown, gfs2 freed quota data objects synchronously without first removing them from the LRU list, so the shrinker (gfs2_qd_shrink_scan) could later traverse the LRU and access already-freed objects, causing a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: Commit message states: "Commit a475c5dd16e5 ... started freeing quota data objects during filesystem shutdown ... but it failed to remove these objects from the LRU list, causing LRU list corruption. This caused use-after-free when the shrinker (gfs2_qd_shrink_scan) tried to access already-freed objects on the LRU list." The fix adds `list_lru_del_obj(&gfs2_qd_lru, &qd->qd_lru);` before `gfs2_qd_dispose(qd)` to ensure removal from the LRU list before freeing.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit a475c5dd16e57c570113eccba51955b5df8bb052
Author: Andreas Gruenbacher <agruenba@redhat.com>
Date:   Wed Aug 23 17:15:47 2023 +0200

    gfs2: Free quota data objects synchronously
    
    In gfs2_quota_cleanup(), wait for the quota data objects to be freed
    before returning.  Otherwise, there is no guarantee that the quota data
    objects will be gone when their kmem cache is destroyed.
    
    Signed-off-by: Andreas Gruenbacher <agruenba@redhat.com>

diff --git a/fs/gfs2/quota.c b/f
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit adds proper handling in qd_put() to dispose quota data synchronously without adding to LRU when SDF_JOURNAL_LIVE is not set (lines 320-330), and in gfs2_quota_cleanup() it marks objects dead, removes them from LRU, and waits for completion (lines 1479-1511). These changes prevent the shrinker from accessing freed objects, thus the vulnerable use-after-free construct is absent.
